summary: Added a new infra/access/osdp package: a pure-Go implementation of the SIA OSDP v2.x wire protocol in CP (Control Panel) mode, plus tools/osdp-sim, a TCP-based OSDP reader (PD) simulator with 17 fault-injection scenarios. This is build-order steps 1-4 of the 6-step plan in docs/MYPINTUSAN_OSDP_PLAN.md for the proposed mypintusan (physical access control) app: framing (crc.go, frame.go, codes.go), a shared PD decoder used by both the simulator and the driver's tests (pd.go), the CP-side polling/state machine and Secure Channel session management (cp.go, bus.go), a TCP transport (transport.go, with serial deferred to step 5), and an OSDP Secure Channel implementation (securechannel.go: AES-128 handshake, per-packet MAC, payload encryption). The design goes through a real fail-closed posture end to end: a door reader that requires Secure Channel and cannot establish or loses it goes out of service and alarms rather than ever falling back to cleartext. No new Go dependencies. There is still no apps/mypintusan and zero application code -- this is infrastructure and a developer tool only, with no consumer yet.
compatibility: No consuming app exists yet, so this cannot affect any shipping product's behavior, config, API, or runtime flow; nothing to migrate. Two things are explicitly caveated as unconfirmed against real hardware rather than presented as production-ready: (1) the CRC byte order on the wire (crc.go, MYPINTUSAN_OSDP_PLAN.md SS2.1/SS6), and (2) the Secure Channel's cryptographic constants -- session-key derivation, cryptogram operand order, MAC chaining, CBC IV -- which were reconstructed from libosdp without the source at hand (securechannel.go's header comment, tools/osdp-sim/README.md). Both require a bench test with a real reader (build-order steps 5-6) before this driver is trusted against hardware; the failure mode if the constants are wrong is loud and safe (the handshake fails and the reader stays out of service), not a silent security downgrade.
